syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Computerised Accounting System: meaning, components, data and information

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the five components of CAS and the role each plays in processing accounting transactions.
Distinguish data from information and recognise the data elements of an accounting transaction.

topics.title: Accounting cycle and salient features of CAS

concepts.learning_objective: Sequence the phases of the accounting cycle that CAS processes.
Recognise the salient features of CAS software: simple and integrated, transparency, accuracy and speed, scalability and reliability.

topics.title: Grouping of accounts and the accounting equation

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the expanded accounting equation Assets = Liabilities + Capital + (Revenues - Expenses).
Classify accounts into the groups and sub-groups used for the Balance Sheet and Statement of Profit and Loss.

topics.title: Codification of accounts and coding structure

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish sequential, block and mnemonic codes and where each is used.
Develop and interpret a hierarchical coding structure and allot codes from it.

topics.title: Using CAS software: security, advantages and limitations

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish one-time activities from recurring activities in using CAS software.
Explain password security, data audit and data vault (encryption) in CAS software.
Evaluate the advantages and limitations of CAS.

topics.title: Accounting Information System and its sub-systems

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the function and reports of each sub-system of the Accounting Information System.
Explain the role of the Management Information System in managerial decision-making.

topics.title: Workbooks, worksheets, cells and cell references

concepts.learning_objective: Identify a workbook, a worksheet, the active worksheet, a cell and a cell address in a spreadsheet.
Distinguish relative, absolute and mixed cell references and predict how each changes when a formula is copied.
Explain how derived values are calculated from basic values and support what-if analysis.

topics.title: Labels, formulas, order of operations and functions

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish labels from formulas and explain how a formula's result can be kept as a fixed value.
Apply the order of mathematical operations that Excel follows when evaluating a formula.
Explain the structure of a function and use named ranges as function arguments.

topics.title: Logical functions: IF, nested IF, AND and OR

concepts.learning_objective: Evaluate the result of an IF function from its logical test and its true and false values.
Trace the result of nested IF functions that test several conditions in turn.
Use AND and OR to combine logical conditions, alone or inside IF.

topics.title: Date and time, mathematical and text functions

concepts.learning_objective: Use TODAY, NOW, DAY, MONTH, YEAR and DATEVALUE and interpret Excel's date serial numbers.
Apply SUMIF, the rounding functions and the COUNT family of functions to business data.
Use TEXT and CONCATENATE to format numbers as text and join text strings.

topics.title: Lookup and reference functions

concepts.learning_objective: Use the vector and array forms of LOOKUP and predict their results, including approximate matches.
Use VLOOKUP and HLOOKUP with the correct arguments and explain their error values.

topics.title: Financial functions

concepts.learning_objective: Use PV, FV and PMT with consistent rate, nper, payment sign and type arguments.
Explain how NPV and RATE work and how NPV differs from PV.

topics.title: Data entry, data validation and formatting

concepts.learning_objective: Describe default data alignment and use the fill handle and Fill Series for fast data entry.
Set data validation rules, input messages and error alerts to keep data accurate.
Apply number formats, merging of cells and other formatting tools to make a worksheet readable.

topics.title: Output reports, data tables, pivot tables and common errors

concepts.learning_objective: Define, extend and clear a print area and print selected ranges of a worksheet.
Use one-variable and two-variable data tables and pivot tables to analyse and summarise data.
Identify the causes of common error values such as #####, #DIV/0!, #N/A and #VALUE! and correct them.

chapters.title: Use of Spreadsheet in Business Applications

topics.title: Payroll accounting and payroll components

concepts.learning_objective: Describe what the preparation of a salary bill provides for, from payroll data to the advice to bank.
Identify earning heads such as Basic Pay, Grade Pay, Dearness Pay, DA, HRA and Transport Allowance.
Distinguish statutory deductions (PT, PF, TDS) from other deductions such as loan and advance recoveries.

topics.title: Elements used in payroll calculation

concepts.learning_objective: Compute the number of effective days present and the Basic Pay Earned for a month.
Calculate total earnings, total deductions and net salary of an employee.

topics.title: Template design for a payroll spreadsheet

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why a spreadsheet's layout and formula cells are planned as a template before data entry.
Apply absolute cell addresses so that references to rate cells do not change when formulas are copied.
Interpret nested IF formulas that assign HRA and Transport Allowance by employee type.

topics.title: Asset accounting and depreciation

concepts.learning_objective: Classify fixed assets as tangible or intangible and recognise the asset categories used in asset accounting.
Explain why depreciation is charged on fixed assets and compute the total depreciation over an asset's life.

topics.title: Depreciation by SLM and WDV methods using SLN and DB

concepts.learning_objective: Use the SLN function with cost to use, salvage value and life to compute straight line depreciation.
Interpret the arguments of the DB function and the formulas used for period and months in the first year.

topics.title: Schedule forming part of the balance sheet

concepts.learning_objective: Compute the closing gross block and accumulated depreciation in a fixed asset schedule.
Compute and interpret the net block as gross block less accumulated depreciation.

topics.title: Loan repayment schedule using PMT

concepts.learning_objective: State the meaning of the Rate, Nper, Pv, Fv and Type arguments of the PMT function.
Write PMT formulas whose rate and number of periods match, to compute loan instalments.

chapters.title: Graphs and Charts for Business Data

topics.title: Graphs and charts: meaning and types

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that a graph is a pictorial representation of data with at least a two-dimensional relationship shown on X and Y axes.
Distinguish a pie chart, which shows sub-groups of a single variable, from a bar diagram, which compares values.

topics.title: Basic steps for preparing a chart in Excel

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how a chart is created in MS Excel 2007 from worksheet data using the Insert tab and Charts group.
Organise and interpret worksheet data, including row and column totals, before plotting it in a chart.

topics.title: Elements of a chart

concepts.learning_objective: Differentiate the chart area from the plot area of 2-D and 3-D charts.
Explain data points, data markers, data series and the legend that identifies them.
Identify the role of chart titles, axis titles and data labels.

topics.title: Formatting and resizing a chart

concepts.learning_objective: Use the Design, Layout and Format tabs of Chart Tools to change the look of chart elements.
Describe how a chart is selected and resized by dragging its corners or borders.

topics.title: Changing the chart type and the pie chart

concepts.learning_objective: State the conditions under which data can be plotted as a pie chart and what its slices represent.
Follow the steps for creating and formatting a 3-D pie chart in Excel.

topics.title: 2-D and 3-D charts, radar and doughnut charts

concepts.learning_objective: Plot independent and dependent values, including negative values, on the X and Y axes around the origin.
Explain the depth (series) axis or Z-axis used in 3-D charts.
Compare radar and doughnut charts with pie charts in terms of axes and data series.

topics.title: Advantages of using graphs and charts

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how graphs help to explore, present and convince.
Evaluate why charts make trends in data easier to grasp than text.
